proofLimits: Actual public workspace/reader browser flows are separate from the previously accepted 72 domain/CLI cases, which are not repeated.
The actual source CLI builds a new owned publication in CI; no app dependency, local build or local browser is used.
All emitted payload files are compared with anonymous served responses before/after. The output manifest has a random buildId: only its closed schema and file/path hashes match semantically.
The provider deployment ID is a metadata label supplied by the parent; byte comparisons do not independently fetch deployment metadata or prove an internal backend identity.
At most one same-origin canonical-path redirect is followed and retained; a direct 404.html response may be 200 or 404 only with exact expected bytes.
Only Playwright1.64.1 is installed in owned runner storage. Chromium Linux packages belong to the disposable runner.
Exit/close/EOF/groups and same-UID owned browser paths plus Linux starttime prove scoped cleanup, not a host-wide inventory.
Narrow Chromium and observed clipboard/storage/download behavior do not establish physical devices, hosted collaboration, npm publication or full reference-product parity.

publication.manifestQualification: buildId is random per build; the served manifest file list and hashes must match, not the random ID or full bytes.

proofLimits: Four authored Chromium journeys; five fresh contexts including one real JavaScript-disabled narrow reader. No physical-device claim.
Projects enter through actual file selection; downloads, native storage, confirmations and clipboard or its visible fallback are observed without API replacements.
Private imported routes may receive the real generated 404 document before the saved local workspace restores; this is not public publication.
No account, upload, backend, provider, model, CLI regression rerun or full Mintlify parity is established.
Browser.close and settled driver operations are recorded here; the outer controller independently verifies owned process absence before removing its scratch.

networkCleanup.basis: Public response bodies cancelled and reader locks released; no host-wide socket inventory.

browserProcessCleanup.basis: Same UID, unique owned-root argv attribution and revalidated Linux kernel PID starttime; no argv/env output.
